newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe vows to dismantle Corsican separatist groups.
newsitem.headline: Juppe vows to dismantle Corsican separatist groups.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe vowed on Monday to "dismantle and put out of action" what he called terrorist groups in Corsica.

After the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) claimed responsibility for a bomb attack on his mayoral office in Bordeaux, Juppe said in a statement the government would act with the same determination it had shown last year against a wave of Algeria-linked bombings.

"The government is determined to combat terrorism in all its forms in Corsica...The police, gendarmerie and justice officials have received the firmest instructions to identify, arrest and try with the full rigour of the law criminals who believe, like real mafias, that they can intimidate and coerce the Republic," a statement from Juppe's office said.
"Those who openly defy the law in Corsca will be fought without weakness or indulgence, The aim is to dismantle and put out of action their networks," it said.

Juppe's office said that by placing bombs in Bordeaux on Saturday and in Aix-en-Provence last month, the FLNC's "historic wing" had shown it was not willing to enter a dialogue offered by the government. Government emissaries are widely reported to have held secret peace talks with the FLNC earlier this year.
"A handful of extremists will not be allowed to impose a reign of terror durably to the detriment of the safety of the (French Mediterranean) island's inhabitants and prosperity," the statement said.
